en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-baoneng-fengpen-jing* (also known as the *Baoliang-gongde-jing*), translated during the Eastern Jin period with the translator’s name lost, records what was thus heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Anāthapiṇḍada Park. Great...

When Maudgalyāyana had first attained the six supernormal powers, wishing to deliver his parents to repay the kindness of their nursing, he immediately surveyed the world with his eye of the Path. He saw that his deceased mother had been reborn among the hungry ghosts, unable to see food or drink, her skin and bones joined together like pillars.
Maudgalyāyana was filled with grief; he immediately filled his alms bowl with rice and went to provide food for his mother.

When his mother received the bowl of rice, she used her left hand to shield the food while attempting to eat with her right hand; however, before the food entered her mouth, it transformed into glowing embers, so that she was ultimately unable to eat.
Maudgalyāyana hurried back to report this to the Buddha, recounting the matter in full detail.
"The roots of your mother's transgressions are deep and firmly entangled; they are beyond what you alone can overcome."
"It must be through the majestic spiritual power of the Sangha that one can attain liberation.
I shall now expound the method of deliverance, so that all who face hardships may be freed from sorrow and suffering."

"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, for the sake of your parents of seven generations who are in distress and difficulty, you should provide parched grain, the five fruits, water jars for irrigation, fragrant oil, courtyard lamps, couches, and bedding; with all that is sweet and delicious in the world, you should make offerings to the Sangha."

On this day, all the assembly of sages—some were in mountain retreats in meditative concentration, some had attained the fruits of the four paths, some were walking in meditation beneath trees, and some had attained the six supernatural powers and could fly through the air—were teaching and transforming śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva manifests through skillful means as a bhikṣu within the great assembly, where all share a single mind in receiving the *pātra* and *bhaṇḍa*.

Possessing the path of the noble community of pure precepts, his virtue is vast and boundless. Should anyone make offerings to such a multitude, their parents of seven generations and five types of relatives shall emerge from the three miserable realms; they shall attain liberation at that very moment, and clothing and food will appear spontaneously.
The Buddha commanded the assembly of monks:
"You should, for the sake of the parents of seven generations of this donor’s family, practice the mind of meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*), and only then partake of this offering.
Maudgalyāyana, the bhikṣus, and the entire assembly rejoiced and respectfully carried out his instructions.
The Sutra on Repaying Kindness through Offering the Alms Bowl, Spoken by the Buddha.
